question: What is the primary goal of the safe motherhood initiative?

options.A: To reduce maternal mortality and morbidity rates
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for caesarean sections
options.C: To promote exclusive formula feeding for newborns
options.D: To increase the birth rate in rural communities

explanation: The core objective of safe motherhood programs is lowering the rates of death and illness related to pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h1)

question: Why do maternal health indicators remain poor in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Too many women refusing to attend any antenatal clinics
options.B: Excessive availability of skilled birth attendants everywhere
options.C: Delayed referrals and limited access to functional facilities
options.D: Strict government bans on traditional birth attendants

explanation: Structural barriers like poor transport, poverty, and delayed clinical referrals heavily contribute to high maternal mortality. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h1)

question: Which supplement is recommended before conception to prevent neural tube defects?
explanation: Early intake of folic acid helps prevent severe birth defects of the brain and spinal cord during embryonic development. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: How does proper birth spacing improve overall maternal health outcomes?

options.A: It ensures that families will only have male children in the future
options.B: It guarantees that the next child will be born without any congenital illness
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any antenatal care visits later
options.D: It allows the mother's body to recover fully from the previous pregnancy

explanation: Adequate spacing restores maternal nutrient stores and physical strength, lowering complication risks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: What is the recommended minimum number of antenatal contacts in a focused ANC model?
explanation: Current global guidelines recommend a minimum of eight antenatal visits to catch and manage complications early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks presents with a sudden severe headache and blurred vision. What condition should the nurse suspect first?
explanation: Headaches and visual disturbances in the third trimester are classic warning signs of rising blood pressure and preeclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h3)

question: What is the leading cause of maternal mortality during childbirth in Nigeria?
explanation: Excessive bleeding after delivery accounts for the highest percentage of maternal deaths across the country. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h4)

question: Why is a uterotonic administered immediately after the delivery of the baby?

options.A: To completely prevent postpartum infection of the wound
options.B: To speed up the delivery of the second twin
options.C: To stimulate uterine contractions and prevent heavy bleeding
options.D: To help the infant initiate spontaneous breathing

explanation: Uterotonics make the uterine muscle clamp down on open blood vessels at the placental site, halting hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h4)

question: Which service is provided at a comprehensive EmONC facility but NOT at a basic EmONC facility?
explanation: Comprehensive centers possess surgical operating theatres and blood banking facilities that basic centers lack. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: What is the most appropriate initial nursing action when a postpartum patient goes into hypovolemic shock?

options.A: Administer oral rehydration salt solutions immediately
options.B: Place the patient in a high Fowler sitting position
options.C: Leave the patient alone to find the attending doctor
options.D: Establish large-bore intravenous access and call for help

explanation: Restoring vascular volume quickly with IV fluids is vital while simultaneously summoning medical assistance for severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: When should breastfeeding ideally be initiated after a normal delivery?

options.A: After the infant receives initial formula
options.B: Within the first hour of life
options.D: Only when the milk comes in fully

explanation: Early breastfeeding fosters bonding, protects against infection through colostrum, and stimulates uterine contraction. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: Why is the immediate 24-hour window following delivery considered a critical period?

options.A: The infant is most likely to develop severe chronic asthma then
options.B: Most maternal and neonatal complications and deaths occur during this time
options.C: Mothers usually experience complete physical recovery within these hours
options.D: Breastfeeding milk production reaches its absolute peak then

explanation: Severe hemorrhage and sudden newborn changes frequently strike within the first day post-delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: What is a primary clinical component of post-abortion care services?

options.A: Discouraging any future use of modern contraceptives
options.B: Emergency treatment of incomplete abortion complications
options.C: Prolonging hospital stay for mandatory moral counseling
options.D: Mandatory reporting of patients to law enforcement agencies

explanation: PAC prioritizes stabilizing the patient and clearing retained products of conception to stop hemorrhage and sepsis. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: Why is contraceptive counseling integrated into routine post-abortion care?

options.A: To permanently sterilize all women who experience a miscarriage
options.B: To help the woman prevent another unintended pregnancy soon
options.C: To test the patient's compliance with clinic instructions
options.D: To prove that the hospital supports family planning policies

explanation: Fertility returns very quickly after pregnancy loss, making immediate family planning crucial for health protection. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: Which duty forms a core part of the nurse's community role in safe motherhood?

options.A: Performing major surgeries in primary health centers
options.B: Conducting outreach to encourage facility-based deliveries
options.C: Enforcing national tax laws on pregnant women
options.D: Financing the construction of new rural hospitals

explanation: Nurses engage communities directly to promote professional care utilization and dispel dangerous myths. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h8)

question: A village nurse discovers that traditional birth attendants are hiding women with prolonged labor. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Call the police to have all traditional birth attendants arrested immediately
options.B: Close down the primary health center in protest against local customs
options.C: Engage the attendants respectfully and teach them urgent referral criteria
options.D: Ignore the practice since community members prefer traditional healers

explanation: Building collaborative relationships and educating traditional birth attendants saves lives by securing timely hospital referrals. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h8)
